description: §17.6.10 / §17.6.4 — a value-form `if` with NO `else`. The trailing `else` is OPTIONAL; when no branch is selected the result is `not`, which renders as NOTHING. `#out-shown` takes the true branch ('YES'); `#out-hidden` selects no branch and renders empty. `#out-cascade-hit` pins that an `else if` cascade with no trailing `else` still selects a matching arm ('mid'); `#out-cascade-miss` pins that falling off the end of such a cascade renders empty. This is a SILENT-WRONG regression guard: before S391 all four of these compiled exit 0 with ZERO diagnostics, emitted the branch value as a dangling no-op expression statement (`"YES";`), and rendered EMPTY on every path — the value was dropped on the floor.
rationale: §17.6.4 had ALREADY ruled the false path: "An if-as-expression without an `else` arm SHALL have an implicit false-path type of `not`" and "The compiler SHALL NOT emit an error or warning for a missing `else` arm." §17.6.10 (S391) makes the rendering consequence explicit: the value-form `if` SHALL NOT require a trailing `else`, and the unselected path SHALL render as nothing. The pre-S391 compiler honoured NEITHER half — it did not render the form AND did not refuse it, because the value-form gate rejected a missing alternate (an artifact of the ternary lowering wanting two arms). Fixed at all three lock-step copies (emit-html `isValueFormIfStmt`, emit-control-flow `_emitIfValueExprInner`, emit-each `_eachValueFormIfRaw`), which emit `""` for the absent arm. No diagnostic is expected on any of the four: §17.6.4 forbids one.
